walk.name: Outlook Drag Enter → HFDrop (Virtual Files) Flow
walk.description: When a user drags an email attachment from Outlook over a Chromium browser window, Windows OLE fires IDropTarget::DragEnter. This walk traces the execution from the COM entry point through the Views/Aura bridge, WebContentsViewAura, DropData preparation (including virtual file extraction for HFDrop), security filtering, and the Mojo IPC call that sends drag metadata to the Blink renderer.

highlights.annotation: COM entry: Windows OLE calls IDropTarget::DragEnter
Notify shell helper for drag-image rendering
Cache the IDataObject (Outlook's data source)
Virtual dispatch → DesktopDropTargetWin::OnDragEnter

cells.narrative: When the user drags an Outlook attachment over Chromium's HWND, Windows OLE calls the COM IDropTarget::DragEnter method. DropTargetWin implements this interface. It first notifies the shell drop-target helper (for rendering the drag image), caches Outlook's IDataObject, and then dispatches to the virtual OnDragEnter which subclasses override. The IDataObject holds all of Outlook's clipboard formats — CF_FILEDESCRIPTOR, CF_FILECONTENTS (TYMED_ISTREAM), and possibly virtual filenames for HFDrop.

data_object.value: <IDataObject* — Outlook's OLE data source with CF_FILEDESCRIPTOR + CF_FILECONTENTS>

highlights.annotation: Virtual dispatch from DropTargetWin resolves here
Translate: wraps IDataObject → OSExchangeData, finds target window

cells.narrative: Virtual dispatch from DropTargetWin::OnDragEnter resolves to DesktopDropTargetWin::OnDragEnter. This is the Views-layer override that bridges Windows COM drag-and-drop into the Aura window system. It delegates all real work to Translate(), which wraps the raw IDataObject into an OSExchangeData, locates the target aura::Window via hit-testing, and calls the DragDropDelegate::OnDragEntered on it.

highlights.annotation: Translate: bridge from Windows COM → Aura
Hit-test: find the aura::Window under cursor
Get DragDropDelegate for the target window
Wrap IDataObject → OSExchangeData (Chromium's platform-neutral drag data)
Dispatch to delegate->OnDragEntered → WebContentsViewAura

cells.narrative: Translate() does the heavy lifting of bridging Windows COM into Aura. It: (1) converts screen pixels to DIP coordinates, (2) hit-tests to find the target aura::Window, (3) gets the DragDropDelegate for that window, (4) wraps the raw IDataObject into an OSExchangeData (Chromium's platform-neutral drag data wrapper — this is what makes Outlook's IStream-based CF_FILECONTENTS accessible via GetVirtualFilenames/GetFileContents), and (5) dispatches OnDragEntered on the delegate. For a browser tab, the delegate is WebContentsViewAura.

highlights.annotation: WebContentsViewAura::OnDragEntered — content-layer entry
Allocate fresh DropData struct
PrepareDropData: extract all clipboard formats from OSExchangeData
Async hit-test: find the RenderWidgetHost under the cursor
Callback: DragEnteredCallback will run when hit-test completes

cells.narrative: WebContentsViewAura::OnDragEntered is the content-layer entry point (called from the Aura delegate dispatch in Translate). It: (1) creates a fresh DropData, (2) calls PrepareDropData to extract all clipboard formats from the OSExchangeData — this is where virtual filenames (HFDrop) are extracted on Windows, (3) notifies the drag_dest_delegate if any (e.g., extensions), and (4) asynchronously hit-tests to find the correct RenderWidgetHost for the cursor position. The actual IPC to the renderer happens in the callback (DragEnteredCallback).

drop_data.value: <DropData — freshly allocated, will be filled by PrepareDropData>

highlights.annotation: PrepareDropData — extract all clipboard formats
Check renderer taint (security: did drag start inside a renderer?)
Extract plain text from IDataObject
Extract URLs
Extract real filenames (e.g., files dragged from Explorer)
HFDrop gate: ShouldIncludeVirtualFiles — only if not renderer-tainted and no URLs
GetVirtualFilenames — Outlook's CF_FILEDESCRIPTOR → virtual file list
Append virtual filenames to drop_data->filenames

cells.narrative: PrepareDropData is where Chromium extracts every clipboard format from the OSExchangeData. For Outlook HFDrop, the critical path is the #if BUILDFLAG(IS_WIN) block at line 750: ShouldIncludeVirtualFiles() returns true when the drag did NOT originate from a renderer and has no URL data. When true, GetVirtualFilenames() reads the CF_FILEDESCRIPTOR clipboard format — this is how Outlook advertises its attachment names (e.g., 'report.pdf'). The actual file bytes aren't available yet (they're behind TYMED_ISTREAM); only the names are extracted here. The bytes will be streamed on actual drop via async retrieval.

drop_data.value: { did_originate_from_renderer: false, is_from_privileged: false, text: "", url_infos: [], filenames: ["attachment.pdf", "report.xlsx"] (virtual) }
drop_data.rationale: Outlook drags are not renderer-tainted, have no URLs, and provide virtual filenames via CF_FILEDESCRIPTOR

highlights.annotation: Async callback: hit-test resolved the target RenderWidgetHost
Mark drag as in-progress
Get the target RenderWidgetHostImpl
Security: validate drag target
FilterDropData: sanitize DropData (strip filenames if renderer-tainted)
Delegate check: allow_drag() — privilege + CanDragEnter
IPC to renderer: DragTargetDragEnter sends DropData metadata to Blink

cells.narrative: DragEnteredCallback fires after the async hit-test completes. It: (1) validates the target RenderWidgetHost for security, (2) stores the drag data and calls FilterDropData to sanitize it — for renderer-tainted drags, filenames are stripped, URLs are filtered, (3) checks the delegate's CanDragEnter to see if the drag is allowed, and (4) makes the critical Mojo IPC call: DragTargetDragEnter sends the DropData metadata to the Blink renderer process. Note: for HFDrop, the filenames list (with virtual entries) goes across to the renderer as metadata — the actual file bytes are still deferred until the user completes the drop.

target_rwh.value: <RenderWidgetHostImpl* — the renderer process host for the active tab>

highlights.annotation: Browser-side IPC entry: receives DropData
Convert DropData → Metadata (strips full data, keeps types + names only)
Mojo IPC: blink_frame_widget_->DragTargetDragEnter sends to renderer

cells.narrative: RenderWidgetHostImpl::DragTargetDragEnter receives the full DropData and immediately converts it to metadata via DropDataToMetaData(). This is a security boundary: the full file bytes never cross to the renderer during drag-enter — only metadata (file names, types, sizes) is sent. The metadata is then forwarded via the blink_frame_widget_ Mojo interface to the renderer process, where Blink's DragController will create a DataTransfer object for JavaScript's dragenter event. For HFDrop, the virtual file names appear in the DataTransfer.items list, but JavaScript cannot read their content until the drop event fires.

metadata.rationale: DropDataToMetaData extracts file names/types but not actual content

changes: DropData converted to Metadata (names only, no bytes)

highlights.annotation: FilterDropData: security sanitization before IPC
Tag with the routing ID of this RenderWidgetHost
Filter all URLs through the process security policy
If drag came from a renderer, strip all filenames (prevent exfiltration)

cells.narrative: FilterDropData is the security sanitization step that runs before the DropData is used for the DragTargetDragEnter IPC. It: (1) tags the data with the routing ID, (2) filters all URLs through the renderer process's security policy (e.g., stripping file:// URLs that the renderer shouldn't know about), and (3) critically — if the drag originated from a renderer (a cross-site drag), it strips ALL filenames to prevent data exfiltration. For Outlook drags, did_originate_from_renderer is false (it came from a native app), so the virtual filenames survive this filter.

drop_data->did_originate_from_renderer.value: false (drag from Outlook, not from a web page)
drop_data->did_originate_from_renderer.rationale: Outlook is a native app, so IsRendererTainted() returned false in PrepareDropData

code.text: // Summary: Outlook DragEnter → HFDrop flow complete.

cells.narrative:
Summary of the Outlook DragEnter → HFDrop flow:

1. **Windows OLE** → DropTargetWin::DragEnter (COM IDropTarget, caches IDataObject)
2. **Virtual dispatch** → DesktopDropTargetWin::OnDragEnter (Views layer)
3. **Translate()** → Wraps IDataObject in OSExchangeData, hit-tests for target aura::Window, dispatches to DragDropDelegate
4. **WebContentsViewAura::OnDragEntered** → Creates DropData, calls PrepareDropData
5. **PrepareDropData** → Extracts all clipboard formats. For HFDrop: ShouldIncludeVirtualFiles() gate passes (not renderer-tainted, no URLs), GetVirtualFilenames() reads CF_FILEDESCRIPTOR from Outlook
6. **Async hit-test** → Finds the correct RenderWidgetHost for the cursor position
7. **DragEnteredCallback** → Validates security, calls FilterDropData (Outlook drags survive since not renderer-tainted), calls DragTargetDragEnter
8. **RenderWidgetHostImpl::DragTargetDragEnter** → Converts DropData to metadata, sends via Mojo IPC to renderer's blink_frame_widget_

Key insight: During drag-enter, only file **names** cross the process boundary — actual bytes from Outlook's TYMED_ISTREAM are deferred until the drop event, where they're asynchronously retrieved via GetVirtualFilesAsTempFiles.
